description: The interim notifier's five-minute window on `published_at` could never fire: `published_at` is the candle's OPEN time, so a signal is already one full period old the instant it exists. Measured live 2026-10-05 -- SUIUSDT M5, published_at 04:20:00Z, written by a pass that finished 04:25:17.1Z, an age of 317s against a 300s window. The window is now a scan bound, the ledger decides what has been handled, and §10.2's freshness is the signal's own TTL. Run from backend/: uv run python -m tests.support.mutation_battery tests/mutations/notifier_lookback.json

mutations.name: the scan bound goes back to the five minutes that could never be met
the scan bound exactly equals H4's period, leaving no room for the pass
the dispatch freshness test never suppresses, so an outage pushes expired signals
freshness is measured against one candle period instead of the TTL -- the same defect, moved
an absent ttl_candles reads as a zero lifetime rather than two candles
an unknown timeframe is guessed at instead of raising
